analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a new 'Close codes and the reconnect wait' section (head lines 173-190) describing provider reconnect-wait behavior by WebSocket close code (1012 service restart versus other codes). The two supplied units are BASE text excerpts (lines 326-950) covering prefix-cache, heartbeat, capacity, inference and models_replace message tables. The added section does not appear in them, and the excerpts contain no changed lines. I reviewed that unchanged context against the patch and found no inconsistency.

Security analysis: the documentation describes a reconnect-wait policy (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy) that reads only the close code, never the reason, and states that every reconnect sends a fresh `register`. This is consistent with the TB-002 and TB-011 model, in which authorization is per-connection and a reconnect does not inherit grants. T-053 (stale authorization surviving a connection change) is unaffected, since the doc says re-registration occurs. The coordinator is trusted, so a 1012 close only shortens the backoff range and does not grow it. A hostile or compromised path could send 1012 repeatedly to cause tight reconnect loops, but the wait is drawn from a range and the coordinator is trusted, so this is low-impact and not supported as a regression. No code, key custody, attestation, cache storage (T-041) or encryption behavior changes. The PR documents provider code (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift) that is not supplied, so I could not verify that the doc matches the implementation. That is a documentation-accuracy question rather than a demonstrated vulnerability. I found no new attack surface.
